battle.name: 第一次進攻燕國
battle.brief: 前226年（秦王政二十一年），秦王命大將王翦率大軍北伐燕國，師次燕郊易水，前鋒逼近燕都薊；燕王喜懼，使使請和、割地納質，秦廷許之，王翦乃退兵。卡面羅馬扭力投石機不在此役現場，秦軍攻城所恃者是弩機、雲梯、撞車與人力拉索式拋石車。

kit.name: 投石機
kit.history: 把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭。攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力。

countries: 交戰的兩方是秦國與燕國。秦始皇二十一年（公元前226年），秦以王翦為主將，統兵自關中及河內、上地一線北上，兵鋒指向燕國都城薊；秦軍沿太行山東麓的平坦地帶推進，前鋒抵達易水流域的燕郊，距薊都只在數十公里之內。燕國此時已是北方僅存的大國，疆域包括今北京市一帶與河北省北部、遼西的邊郡，國都薊兼是北方遊牧地帶與中原農耕地帶的交會點；燕王喜依靠燕國原有的步兵、弓弩手與城防體系固守薊城，同時向秦軍請和，願割地納質。秦廷對此有兩種取向：一派認為燕王既然請和、肯割地，便可藉此省兵；另一派則主張大軍既然已陳於城下，應乘勢攻取。此役牽涉的第三方並非聯軍，而是北方草原的壓力：燕國在北面設上谷、漁陽、右北平、遼西諸邊郡，抵禦匈奴與東胡的侵擾，一旦燕亡，這道屏障也會隨之瓦解。可以說，第一次進攻燕國是一場由秦國主導、燕國被動應對的單向施壓行動；大軍开到城下，卻沒有把會戰真正打下來，兩國都保留了餘地。
countriesEn: The two sides were the state of Qin and the state of Yan. In the twenty-first year of the reign of Qin Shi Huang (226 BC), Qin appointed the general Wang Jian as commander and marched north with a great army drawn from the Guanzhong base as well as the Henan and Shangdi regions, aiming at Yan's capital at Ji. The Qin column advanced along the open ground on the eastern foot of the Taihang range and its vanguard reached Yan Jiao in the basin of the Yi River, only several dozen kilometres short of the capital. Yan was by then the largest of the surviving northern states, holding the area of present-day Beijing together with the northern part of Hebei and the Liaoxi border commanderies; its capital Ji stood where the pastoral lands of the north met the agricultural lands of the central plain. King Xi of Yan relied on the existing infantry, crossbowmen and the defensive system of the city to hold Ji, while at the same time sending envoys to the Qin army to ask for peace and to offer ceded territory and hostages. The Qin court had two reactions: Chancellor Li Si and others favoured accepting the submission and settling the matter without further war, while the Qin king weighed Yan's apparent sincerity against its behaviour and in the end allowed relations to resume and ordered Wang Jian to stand down. The third party in this affair was not an allied coalition but pressure from the northern steppe: Yan had established the border commanderies of Shanggu, Yuyang, Youbeiping and Liaoxi to hold off Xiongnu and Donghu raids, and once Yan fell that screen would fall with it. The first attack on Yan was thus a one-sided act of coercion led by Qin, with Yan forced into a passive response; the army reached the walls, yet no decisive battle was fought, and both sides kept room to manoeuvre.
people: 關鍵人物分屬兩邊。秦方由秦始皇嬴政直接統御，這一步是他完成統一大業的倒數。主將王翦是滅趙、滅楚兩役的名將，出兵時已六十餘歲，仍是秦廷倚重的宿將；他按兵不進、以大軍列於燕郊而不出手的處置，正是全役的樞紐，也讓秦國免去在薊城堅城之下硬攻的風險。李斯是秦廷中主理對燕文移與議和的臣僚之一，出身荀卿門下，以書寫辯說見長；真正決定攻燕節奏的仍是秦王本人。燕方的主君燕王喜在秦軍壓境時選擇求和割地，而他身邊的太子丹走的是另一條路：丹曾質於秦，逃亡回燕後一心報秦，收留了自秦國逃出的將領樊於期，鍛造淬毒的匕首，計畫以荊卿與燕國少年秦舞陽入秦行刺。荊卿本為衛國人，後來到燕國，與高漸離齊名的擊筑藝人，往來燕趙之間；秦舞陽年方十三便敢殺人，燕人無不畏其目光。兩人於前227年（秦王政二十年，一般繫於此年）行刺失敗，秦王震怒，燕國自此再無退路。
peopleEn: The key figures fall on both sides. On the Qin side the campaign was directed personally by the Qin king, Ying Zheng, since this step was the countdown to the completion of unification. The commander was Wang Jian, the general who had destroyed Zhao and Chu; already past sixty when he took command, he remained the veteran on whom the court relied. His decision to hold the army in place at Yan Jiao instead of striking was the hinge of the whole operation, and it spared Qin the cost of battering a stubborn city at Ji. Chancellor Li Si handled the negotiations with Yan over a long period and after the first attack favoured using the truce to pin Yan down, though the Qin king himself remained the one who set the tempo of the war against Yan. On the Yan side the ruler, King Xi, chose to seek peace and cede land when the Qin army appeared, while his crown prince Dan took a different road. Dan had been a hostage in Qin and had escaped back to Yan, and he was determined to strike back; he harboured the Qin general Fan Yuqi, who had fled to Yan, had a poisoned dagger fashioned, and planned to send Jing Ke together with the Yan youth Qin Wuyang to Qin to assassinate the king. Jing Ke was originally a man of Wey who had later moved to Yan, and was known alongside the zither-player Gao Jianli; Qin Wuyang was only thirteen and had already killed a man, and no one in Yan dared meet his eye. Their attempt failed in 227 BC (generally dated to the twentieth year of the Qin king), the Qin king was furious, and Yan lost its last way out.
kits: 卡面上的投石機（Onager）是羅馬式的單臂扭力拋石機，靠扭力簧束儲存的彈簧勢能推動一根長臂，臂端以皮兜裝石，整具機架承受反力；它代表的是攻城器械中破壞力最可觀的一類，也就是把計算過的動能直接砸在城牆上。不過這件兵器並不在前226年的燕國戰場上，秦國的攻城器械另有體系。與投石機功能相對應的，是中國記載中的拋石機：戰國晚出的《墨子》城篇論守城時提到以礮石擊敵，漢代文獻所稱的「霹靂車」則屬拉索式，以整組人力拉起長臂、臂端繫兜拋石，動力來源與結構都與羅馬的扭力機不同，兩者只在「以拋擲打擊城垣與塔樓」這件事上同類。秦軍真正攜帶並用於攻城的，是可折疊推前的雲梯與飛樓、可反覆撞擊城門的撞車，以及配合作戰的弩機——秦弩是本役最具殺傷力的攻城手段，單兵可攜、操作簡易，箭鏃多為銅或鐵質。軍中近戰裝備以鐵矛、劍、戈、戟與皮甲、札甲為主，野戰與攻城都配置輕車與輜重車，由牛馬挽曳。除器械本身外，秦軍的真正優勢更多來自組織與後勤：關中糧秣、徭發兵員、按斬首計功的賞格、驛傳與嚴整的軍令，構成遠征得以維持的條件。
kitsEn: The onager on the card is a Roman single-arm torsion stone-thrower: a bundle of twisted skeins stores the spring power that drives a long throwing arm, a sling at the arm's tip carries the stone, and the whole frame absorbs the reaction. It represents the most destructive family of siege engines, the one that hurls calculated kinetic energy straight into a wall. It was not, however, present on the battlefield of Yan in 226 BC, and the Chinese siege-engine tradition was a separate system. The counterpart to the onager in Chinese records is the stone-throwing engine: the late Warring States text Mozi discusses hurling stones with projectile engines in its chapter on defending a city, while the machine the Han texts call the thunder-thunder chariot belongs to the traction family, with a crew hauling a long arm by ropes and a sling at its tip; its source of power and its structure differ from the Roman torsion engine, and the two are akin only in the business of throwing stones and shot at walls and towers. What the Qin army actually carried and used in the attack were folding scaling ladders and movable turret towers, battering rams for the gates, and the crossbow engines worked alongside them; the Qin crossbow was the most lethal siege instrument of the campaign, carried by a single soldier, simple to operate, and firing bronze or iron-headed bolts. Close combat was fought with iron-tipped spears, swords, ge, halberds, and leather and lamellar armour, and both field and siege columns used light wagons and baggage carts drawn by oxen and horses. Beyond the machines themselves, the real advantage of the Qin army lay in organisation and logistics: grain from Guanzhong, conscripted levies, rewards reckoned by decapitation, the relay stations, and strict military discipline were what made a distant expedition possible.
tactics: 本役的戰術核心是「壓而不用兵」。秦滅六國的次序是先韓、再趙、再魏、再楚，最後才是燕與齊；先消滅近鄰、孤立遠國，是秦自商鞅變法以來確立的戰略。到燕國時秦已無後顧，於是由王翦率大軍沿太行山東麓北上，不走險峻山道，取能供大軍展開與給養的平原通道，進抵易水流域的燕郊。抵達之後秦軍列陣而駐，不急攻、不合戰，僅以大軍存在的壓力逼燕王議和，等於以進軍速度代替攻城戰。這一步的算盤很清楚：薊城池堅牆厚、糧草可支撐，強攻代價大；燕國若肯割地，則可兵不血刃地取得北方的屏障與通道，兵鋒得以轉向最後的齊國。燕方的應對則是外交與暗殺並行，一面遣使至秦軍前請和、割城納質，一面由太子丹在薊城策劃刺秦，試圖以一次成功的暗襲換取喘息。燕軍在易水一線設防，重點放在城防與道路遲滯，而不是與秦軍在野外交鋒。補給上，秦軍糧秣依河內、上地的轉輸線供給，隊伍配置大量輜重車與隨軍牲畜；燕國則倚仗邊郡的畜產與薊城的囤糧應付長期對峙。最終秦軍在取得燕王讓步的承諾後退回本土，全役沒有爆發決定性會戰。
tacticsEn: The tactical heart of this campaign was pressure applied without a set-piece battle. Qin's order of conquest ran through Han, then Zhao, then Wei, then Chu, with Yan and Qi left for last; eliminating the near neighbours first and isolating the far ones had been Qin's strategic doctrine since the reforms of Shang Yang. By the time he turned on Yan there was nothing behind Qin, so Wang Jian took the great army north along the eastern foot of the Taihang, avoided the steep defiles, chose the plain road that could carry a host and its supply columns, and came up to Yan Jiao in the basin of the Yi River. Having arrived, the army arrayed itself and stood: no assault, no engagement, and nothing but the weight of the host pressing the king of Yan into negotiations. The arithmetic was plain. Ji was a city with thick walls and stores that could hold out; a storm of the walls would have been expensive. If Yan would cede land, Qin could take the northern screen and the corridor beyond it without the loss of men, and turn its army on the last of the enemies, Qi. Yan answered with diplomacy and conspiracy at once: envoys went forward to the Qin ranks to ask for peace and offer towns and hostages, while in the capital the crown prince plotted the assassination of the Qin king, hoping a single successful ambush would buy the state a respite. Yan's troops were posted along the Yi River, and the emphasis was on the city defences and on slowing the roads, not on meeting the Qin army in open field. On the Qin side, grain and stores travelled by the relay of Henan and Shangdi, and the column carried a great many baggage carts and draught animals; Yan relied on the animal wealth of its border commanderies and on the grain stacked in Ji to sustain a long standoff. In the end the Qin army withdrew to its own territory once it had secured Yan's concessions, and no decisive engagement was ever fought.
data: 可核對的數字分屬三個層次。其一是時間軸：第一次進攻燕國發生於秦王政二十一年，即公元前226年；次年即前227年，太子丹遣荊卿刺秦；前225年秦軍再興，燕都薊被攻下，燕王喜出奔遼東；前222年秦軍平定遼東，燕王喜被俘，燕國遂亡；前221年秦王政稱始皇帝，統一完成。秦滅六國的次序與年份為韓前230、趙前228、魏前225、楚前223、燕前222、齊前221，先近後遠共歷七年。其二可確定的是兵員的量級而非確數：本役秦軍人數在傳世文獻中記載有限且互有出入，能肯定的是秦國仍具備一次投入數十萬人的國家組織能力——同期伐楚之役《史記》記王翦率兵六十萬；而燕國久戰之後兵源有限，總人口遠小於秦，故只能以守城待變。其三是地理與距離：秦軍自河內、上地一線出師，至燕郊前線，以今地里程計約五百至六百公里；燕郊至薊都約六十公里上下，一日急行軍即可抵達，故秦軍的逼近本身即是施壓手段；易水距薊亦不過數十公里，歷來是燕軍北拒的天然界線。人物方面，王翦以六十餘歲之齡仍受命統兵，滅趙、滅楚皆其手筆，伐燕之後受封武成侯，約卒於前221年統一告成之時。至於確切月份，現存史籍只存年份不存月，檔案中的起始月份取秦軍秋季出師、冬季前完成部署的常例。
dataEn: The verifiable figures fall into three groups. First, the chronology: the first attack on Yan took place in the twenty-first year of the Qin king, that is 226 BC; a year later, in 227 BC, the crown prince sent Jing Ke to assassinate the Qin king; in 225 BC the Qin army returned, took the capital of Ji and the king of Yan fled east to Liaodong; in 222 BC the Qin army pacified Liaodong, King Xi was taken prisoner and the state of Yan ceased to exist; in 221 BC the Qin king took the title of First Emperor and the unification was complete. The order and dates of the conquest of the six states were Han 230, Zhao 228, Wei 225, Chu 223, Yan 222 and Qi 221 BC — seven years from the near to the far. Second, the scale of the armies rather than exact figures: the numbers for the Qin force in this campaign are thinly recorded and inconsistent in the transmitted texts, but what can be certain is that Qin still possessed the organisation of a state able to commit several hundred thousand men at once, since the contemporary campaign against Chu is recorded in the Shiji as Wang Jian leading six hundred thousand; Yan, exhausted by long war, had a much smaller population and could only shut up its cities and wait. Third, geography and distance: the Qin army set out from the Henan and Shangdi lines, and the march to the Yan Jiao front lay about five to six hundred kilometres as the land is measured today; from Yan Jiao to the capital of Ji is some sixty kilometres, a single day's forced march, so the proximity of the Qin army was itself the instrument of coercion; the Yi River, some tens of kilometres from Ji, had always been the natural line on which Yan set its northern defence. As for persons, Wang Jian was still given command in his sixties; he had destroyed Zhao and Chu, and after this campaign against Yan he was ennobled as Marquis of Wucheng, dying in 221 BC. As to the exact month, the surviving histories keep the year but not the month, and the starting month entered in the record follows the normal practice of a Qin army setting out in the autumn to complete its deployment before winter.
cause: 打起嚟的根由有遠因近因兩層。遠因是秦滅六國的整體戰略：自商鞅變法之後，秦以耕戰立國，把土地與軍功制度化，滅魏、趙、楚之後，北方只剩燕與齊兩個舊諸侯。燕國地處秦的北面，憑太行山與渤海之險，本是秦向東推進與北方遊牧地帶交通之間的緩衝，秦要完成統一，就必須先拔掉燕。近因則是燕秦關係在最後階段的破裂：燕王喜一面屢次遣使請和、割地求全，一面收留自秦逃亡的將領樊於期，太子丹又質秦而歸，在燕都籌劃報秦之舉，鍛造淬毒的匕首，選荊卿與秦舞陽為刺客，只等秦王東巡歸途便要下手。燕國的「恭順」與「陰謀」同時存在，使秦廷無法再相信一份和約可以維持。於是秦王政決定在轉向齊國之前，先以大軍把燕國壓服；前227年刺秦失敗，更使任何和議都告破裂，直接導致前225年的第二次進攻。也就是說，第一次進攻燕國本身並非由某一場具體衝突引發，而是秦國統一大業的倒數計時，也是燕國用拖延外交、以暗殺搏命的最後機會。
causeEn: There were both a remote cause and an immediate one. The remote cause was the overall strategy of Qin's destruction of the six states: after the reforms of Shang Yang, Qin had built a state on agriculture and war, institutionalising land grants and military merit, and after Wei, Zhao and Chu had fallen only Yan and Qi remained in the north. Yan lay to the north of Qin, protected by the Taihang mountains and the Bohai, and served as a buffer between Qin's eastward road and the pastoral routes of the steppe; to complete the unification Qin had to remove Yan first. The immediate cause lay in the breakdown of relations in the final stage: King Xi repeatedly sent envoys to sue for peace and offered land, yet at the same time the state sheltered the general Fan Yuqi, who had fled Qin, and the crown prince, having been a hostage in Qin and escaped home, nursed a plan of revenge in the capital, had a poisoned dagger made and chosen Jing Ke and Qin Wuyang as his assassins, waiting only for the Qin king's return from an eastern tour. Yan's simultaneous posture of obedience and conspiracy made it impossible for the Qin court to believe any treaty would hold. The Qin king therefore decided to crush Yan with an army before turning on Qi; and the failure of the assassination in 227 BC destroyed any possibility of a lasting truce and led directly to the second attack in 225 BC. The first attack on Yan, in other words, was not triggered by any single incident but was the countdown of Qin's unification and Yan's last chance to buy time by procrastination and by conspiracy.
impact: 第一次進攻燕國沒有帶來戰果上的改變，帶來的是政治上的連鎖反應。對秦國而言，此役以一次成功的戰略進逼換來燕國的割地與復交，王翦得以保全大軍、避免在薊城堅城之下消耗兵力，把完整的軍力留給齊國；秦廷由此看到，北方燕國可以不打而服。對燕國而言，這一年是災難性的：太子丹把秦國的善意當成軟弱，用一次失敗的刺秦換來了秦王更盛的怒火，第二次進攻燕國隨即把燕都薊付諸兵火，燕王喜從遼西節節退到遼東，最終在前222年被俘。對北方邊疆格局而言，燕國在上谷、漁陽、右北平、遼西諸郡的設防是秦與匈奴、東胡之間的一道緩衝；燕亡之後這道屏障消失，匈奴得以重新南下河套，促成秦王政在統一後不久派蒙恬率三十萬眾北逐匈奴、修築長城並經營河南地的局面。對後世而言，這場戰役常被記為秦以不戰而屈人之兵對待北方邊國的樣本，也說明了一次刺秦失敗如何把原本可以用談判收束的衝突推成全面戰爭。
impactEn: The first attack on Yan changed nothing on the field, but it set off a chain of political consequences. For Qin the operation bought Yan's cession and the resumption of relations at the price of a single strategic advance; Wang Jian kept his army intact, avoided grinding it away against the walls of Ji, and preserved his full strength for Qi. The court drew the lesson that the northern state of Yan could be reduced without a battle. For Yan that year was disastrous: the crown prince took Qin's courtesy for weakness and exchanged a single failed ambush for the Qin king's fiercer anger, and the second attack soon put the capital of Ji to the torch, driving King Xi east by stages until his capture in 222 BC. For the northern frontier, the chain of commanderies at Shanggu, Yuyang, Youbeiping and Liaoxi had been the screen between Qin and the Xiongnu and Donghu; with Yan gone the screen disappeared, the Xiongnu were able to move south again into the Hetao region, and this prompted the Qin king not long after the unification to send Meng Tian with three hundred thousand men to drive the Xiongnu north, build the long wall and administer the lands south of the Yellow River. For later ages this campaign is often cited as a model of Qin's way of bringing a northern state to terms without a war, and as a demonstration of how one failed assassination could turn a conflict that might have been closed by negotiation into a general war.
result: 全役的結局是一場沒有交戰的勝利與一次沒有勝利的和平。前226年秦軍抵達燕郊之後，燕王喜派使者到秦軍前請和，願割城邑、納質子，秦廷應允，兩國暫時復交，王翦奉詔退兵：燕國保住了薊都與既有疆土，秦軍則沒有攻破任何一座燕城。從秦的目標看，北方最後一個大敵尚未消滅，統一只完成到五家，齊國仍在東方獨存；但從戰略看，秦以最小代價換得燕國的讓步，把兵力完整保留下來。對燕國而言，這是延續而非解決：前227年刺秦失敗後，秦國再興大軍，前225年攻下燕都，燕王喜出奔遼東，前222年遼東平定，燕王喜被俘，燕國正式滅亡；次年即前221年，齊王建降，六國盡滅，秦王政改稱皇帝，郡縣制推行於全國。所以第一次進攻燕國的真正結果，是把一場可以由割地了結的邊疆衝突推成了秦統一的倒數第二場戰爭，並為秦軍最終攻取薊城、隨後北擊匈奴鋪平了道路。
resultEn: The outcome of the whole operation was a victory without a battle and a peace without a win. When the Qin army reached Yan Jiao in 226 BC, King Xi sent envoys forward to ask for peace, offering towns and hostages; the Qin court agreed, the two states resumed relations for the time being, and Wang Jian withdrew under orders. Yan kept its capital of Ji and its existing territory, and the Qin army took not a single Yan city. Judged by Qin's own aims, the last great enemy in the north was still standing and the unification had been achieved only against five of the six, with Qi still solitary in the east; judged strategically, however, Qin had won Yan's concessions at the smallest price and kept its army whole. For Yan this was postponement rather than settlement: after the assassination failed in 227 BC the Qin court raised a new army, took the capital in 225 BC, drove King Xi out to Liaodong, and in 222 BC pacified Liaodong and took the king prisoner, so that Yan formally ceased to exist; the following year, 221 BC, King Jian of Qi surrendered, the last of the six was gone, the Qin king took the title of emperor and the commandery-and-county system was carried out across the realm. The real result of the first attack on Yan, then, was to turn a frontier conflict that could have been closed by a cession into the penultimate war of the Qin unification, and to clear the way for the final taking of Ji and for the subsequent drive against the Xiongnu.
